top_stories.title: BigBear Microsoft 365 phishing service bypassed MFA at 258 organizations
top_stories.summary: A phishing-as-a-service framework called BigBear 2.0 successfully bypassed multi-factor authentication at 258 organizations, stealing over 5,000 Microsoft 365 credentials. The attacks demonstrate adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) techniques capable of circumventing MFA protections on Microsoft 365 accounts.

top_stories.title: IDScan sued over alleged data breach affecting 153 million drivers
top_stories.summary: IDScan, an identity verification company, faces multiple lawsuits after hackers allegedly breached its systems and offered to sell data from more than 153 million driver's licenses. The breach targets a company whose core business is identity document scanning and verification services.

top_stories.title: Microsoft’s September Identity Batch Proves the Authentication Gap Is Not an Open-Source Problem
top_stories.summary: Microsoft disclosed nine vulnerabilities outside its standard Patch Tuesday cycle on September 3, 2026, including two CVSS 10.0-rated flaws: CVE-2026-83711, an authorization bypass in Azure AD B2C, and CVE-2026-70352. The disclosures directly affect Microsoft's identity platform and carry maximum severity ratings, implicating Azure AD B2C authentication and authorization mechanisms.

top_stories.title: Critical Citrix NetScaler auth bypass now leveraged in attacks
top_stories.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler (CVE-2026-19490) is being actively exploited in the wild. The flaw allows attackers to bypass authentication controls, with exploitation activity confirmed by vulnerability intelligence firm Previdian.

top_stories.title: Fake IT Calls Target Executives in Microsoft 365 Data Theft and Extortion Attacks
top_stories.summary: A threat campaign is targeting executives by combining IT help desk vishing, adversary-in-the-middle token theft, and residential-proxy sign-ins to compromise Microsoft 365 and other SaaS accounts. The attacks focus on stealing session tokens to bypass MFA, with victims primarily being directors, vice presidents, and other senior staff.

news.title: Product showcase: Doppler secures secrets for humans, pipelines, and AI agents
news.summary: Doppler has published a product showcase highlighting its secrets management platform's capabilities for securing credentials across human users, CI/CD pipelines, and AI agents. The platform addresses the challenge of managing secrets for automated identities created by AI coding agents and MCP servers that access databases, cloud providers, and internal APIs.

news.title: Zero trust AI agents demand a different kind of security
news.summary: Teleport VP of Product Marketing Chris Webber argues that zero trust principles require rethinking for AI agents, citing limitations of traditional least privilege and point-in-time verification approaches. Teleport's approach involves trusted runtimes with zero starting privileges and real-time identity security monitoring of agent behavior.

news.title: JSCeal Malware Can Bypass Google Authentication Using Stolen Session Cookies
news.summary: Check Point Research has analyzed JSCeal, a compiled V8 JavaScript malware capable of bypassing Google authentication by stealing session cookies. The malware features credential harvesting, surveillance, and traffic-interception capabilities, with payloads protected using RC4-encrypted strings, control-flow flattening, and proxy functions.

news.title: The End of the Authentication Gap: Microsoft’s SSPR Enforcement
news.summary: Microsoft Entra ID will enforce a policy change effective September 7, 2026, retiring the use of unregistered directory contact data for self-service password reset (SSPR). Mobile numbers, business phones, and secondary emails must be explicitly registered as authentication methods for SSPR to function, eliminating reliance on unverified directory contact information.

news.title: Okta Jumps 20% as AI-Driven Security Fears Fuel a Beat-and-Raise Quarter
news.summary: Okta shares surged up to 29% after the company beat fiscal Q2 earnings estimates, with adjusted EPS of $1.05 versus $0.97 expected and revenue of $805 million representing 11% growth. The company also issued a raise in forward guidance, with AI-driven security concerns cited as a demand driver for Okta's identity security platform.

news.title: Attackers Breached JetBrains Cadence via Unpatched TeamCity, Extracting AWS Credentials
news.summary: Threat actors exploited a critical vulnerability in JetBrains' TeamCity to breach the Cadence environment and extract AWS credentials. JetBrains is urging affected Cadence users to immediately revoke and rotate all credentials and secrets used in their Cadence executions.

news.title: zitadel v4.17.3
news.summary: ZITADEL released version 4.17.3 of its open-source identity and access management platform. The platform supports SSO, MFA, passkeys, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, and multi-tenant access control.

news.title: Pathlock Recognized as a Representative Vendor in the 2026 Gartner® Market Guide for Identity Governance and Administration
news.summary: Pathlock has been named a Representative Vendor in the 2026 Gartner Market Guide for Identity Governance and Administration. The recognition highlights Pathlock's position in the IGA market, with the report focusing on emerging risks and opportunities in the evolving IGA landscape.

news.title: Adobe Names New CEO As Earnings Approach And AI Fears Persist; Navan, SailPoint Also Due
news.summary: The article covers broad software sector market movements, mentioning SailPoint alongside Adobe and Navan in the context of upcoming earnings reports. SailPoint's inclusion appears to be a minor reference within a wider financial markets roundup rather than substantive IAM-specific news.

news.title: Thomson Reuters Court Software Breach May Have Exposed SSNs and Sealed Data
news.summary: Thomson Reuters disclosed that an unauthorized party accessed files from C-Track, its West Publishing court case management platform, in March 2026, affecting courts across 11 U.S. states, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Ontario, Canada. The breach potentially exposed sensitive court records including individuals' names and Social Security Numbers, with the intrusion discovered on June 30, 2026.

news.title: Shai-Hulud's Reach Just Grew to 469 Credential Locations. Here's What That Means
news.summary: A new variant of the Shai-Hulud infostealer worm has expanded its credential scanning capability from 189 to 469 locations, targeting developer environments, CI/CD tooling, cloud configurations, and AI tool configs. GitGuardian researchers discovered the evolution in early August, highlighting an increased threat to stored credentials across a wide range of infrastructure targets.

news.title: Microsoft Security enhancements: Defender MDR Plan 2, Entra Tenant Governance, Intune Autopilot, Purview Auto-Labeling, and AI Agent Containment
news.summary: Microsoft has released a set of security enhancements including Entra Tenant Governance for multi-tenant identity governance management. Additional updates include Defender MDR Plan 2 for third-party log detection, Intune Autopilot improvements, Purview auto-labeling throughput increases, and AI agent containment guidance.

news.title: An infostealer log can bypass MFA—respond within the first hour
news.summary: The article addresses how infostealer logs can capture active browser sessions and identity-provider tokens, effectively bypassing MFA protections. Security teams are advised to treat compromised credentials from infostealer logs as potential live identity compromises requiring response within the first hour.

news.title: Old, Unpatched Flaws Give Attackers Access to Philippines Nuclear Agency
news.summary: Threat actors exploited unpatched vulnerabilities in ownCloud to breach the Philippines Nuclear Agency, stealing credential stores, personnel records, and reactor databases. The attack leveraged commodity vulnerabilities to gain initial access, resulting in the compromise of authentication credentials and sensitive identity-related data.

news.title: Attackers Pounce on Critical Artifactory Bug Following Disclosure
news.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-82329) has been disclosed in JFrog Artifactory, allowing attackers to gain admin-level access on affected systems. Exploitation attempts followed shortly after public disclosure of the flaw.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web service is selling digital scans of over 153 million U.S. and Canadian drivers licenses, apparently sourced from a Louisiana-based identity verification company. The FBI's New Orleans field office has opened an official inquiry into the breach.

news.title: Anthropic Users Hit by Infostealer Attacks, Session Thefts
news.summary: A threat actor deployed infostealer malware to steal session tokens and gain unauthorized access to Anthropic Claude user accounts. The attack highlights session hijacking as an authentication bypass technique, circumventing credential-based controls by stealing active session data.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Canadian cybercriminal Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges related to hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake cloud storage. The attacks involved unauthorized access to customer accounts, stealing data including over 100 million AT&T customer call and text records.

news.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
news.summary: CISA published a postmortem on a data breach in which a contractor exposed dozens of internal credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, in a public GitHub repository for nearly six months. The incident highlights credential management and secrets management failures, with security experts identifying gaps in CISA's detection and response processes.
